target.title: fix(onepassword): key pending authorizations by tool call id only
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Live verification of the `onepassword` plugin on a production gateway showed every `get` failing closed with `POLICY_NOT_EVALUATED`, including `auto`-policy slugs. The broker correlated its `before_tool_call` authorization with the later tool execution via a key built from (agentId, sessionKey, sessionId, toolCallId) — but core sources the hook context and the execute context independently, and they disagree on session fields in production. Unit tests drove both sides with one consistent context and could not catch it.

Refs #105924; follow-up to #106133. Live evidence: production audit rows with `errorCode: POLICY_NOT_EVALUATED` for auto-tier gets while the approve tier correctly raised approvals on the same install.

## Why This Change Was Made

Neither candidate key is safe: session fields mismatch across the hook/execute boundary, and provider tool-call ids are not globally unique (local runtimes emit sequential ids like `call_0`, so toolCallId-only keying would collapse concurrent sessions). Instead the hook now mints a fresh UUID per call and returns it through the hook's adjusted `params` — the one value core guarantees to hand unchanged to the tool handler, on both the direct and the approval-resolved path. `get()` resolves the pending authorization by that nonce only.

Security properties, each covered by a test:
- Immune to hook/execute context asymmetry (production regression test).
- Concurrent sessions reusing the same provider tool-call id stay isolated (each gets its own nonce).
- Model-supplied `authorizationNonce` values are always overwritten by the hook and never resolve; entries are single-consumption and TTL-bounded; slug/reason are still cross-checked; missing nonce fails closed.

Also surfaces `errorCode` in `openclaw onepassword audit` output — the field existed in stored rows but the CLI projection dropped it, which made the live diagnosis needlessly hard.

## User Impact

The plugin's `get` action works on real gateways instead of failing closed on every call. Audit output now shows error codes. Tool schema gains an internal optional `authorizationNonce` param (documented as gateway-injected); no config changes.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/onepassword`: 6 files, 55 tests pass, including three new adversarial tests (asymmetric contexts, colliding tool-call ids across sessions, forged nonce rejection).
- Root cause traced on a live production gateway (managed deployment build of main incl. #106133): auto-tier `get` audit rows show `POLICY_NOT_EVALUATED` pre-fix; the hook side demonstrably runs (approve tier raised a real approval prompt on the same install).
- Core contract verified: `hookResult.params` merges into the executed params after approval resolution (`src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts` finalParams path).

target.title: fix(gateway): bound BOOT.md file read size
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadBootFile` in `src/gateway/boot.ts` read the workspace `BOOT.md` with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, allowing an arbitrarily large file to be loaded into memory during gateway boot.

## Why This Change Was Made

Switch to `readRegularFile` from `../infra/regular-file.js` with a 16 MiB cap, matching the pattern used for other bounded file reads. target.title: fix: tighten findSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer with execution guard
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `findSchema.limit` accepts floating-point values via `Type.Number()`, but "Max results" is inherently an integer-valued field. Float values like `limit=5.5` silently pass `Type.Number` validation and reach tool execution with ambiguous behavior.

**Solution**: Tighten `limit` to `Type.Integer()` with a runtime `Number.isSafeInteger` execution guard. **Per ClawSweeper review, `minimum: 1` has been removed** — zero and negative values retain the existing runtime normalization behavior, so the change only rejects fractional (non-integer) values.

**What changed / NOT changed**:
1. Schema: `Type.Number()` → `Type.Integer()` (no minimum constraint)
2. Runtime: `Number.isSafeInteger(limit)` guard rejects non-integer at execution boundary
3. Focused regression tests (10 cases): valid int, float rejection, zero/negative acceptance (preserved normalization), optional, required pattern, execution boundary
4. Root proof script removed per ClawSweeper review

The runtime `Number.isSafeInteger` guard rejects fractional values at the tool-call boundary. `normalizePositiveLimit` handles value clamping. Zero and negative values continue to be normalized at runtime (existing behavior preserved).

**merge-risk declaration**: Low — schema + guard change to internal tool parameter. Only fractional values are rejected; zero and negative values retain existing runtime normalization. No session state, auth, message delivery, or security boundary involved.

## Tests and validation

- `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` → exit 0 ✓

target.title: fix(memory): hide QMD transport metadata from recalled content
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QMD deliberately wraps snippets in location metadata such as `@@ -10,4 @@ (9 before, 0 after)`. Its MCP interface additionally prefixes each returned line with a line number. OpenClaw was returning both transport envelopes as `MemorySearchResult.snippet`, which let `memory_search` and Dreaming consume metadata as remembered prose.

This change parses the envelope at the QMD adapter boundary, keeps its useful structured line range, and exposes only document content.

Related: #106937
Related: #89444, #71030

## Why

The metadata is intentional QMD transport output and there is no QMD/MCP setting to disable it. Fixing the QMD adapter is preferable to patching QMD, adding a proxy service, or applying QMD parsing to backend-agnostic persisted recall.

The parser is deliberately conservative:

- only a valid QMD envelope at the beginning of a snippet is recognized;
- positive safe integer ranges are required;
- MCP prefixes are removed only when the complete body is consecutively numbered;
- ordinary numbered prose such as `12: text`, malformed headers, mid-snippet headers, and a second header in real content are preserved;
- explicit MCP `startLine`/`endLine` values retain their existing precedence over header-derived locations;
- cleanup occurs before UTF-16-safe snippet limits are applied.

Historical recall-store migration is intentionally out of scope. The shared recall normalizer remains backend-agnostic and does not parse QMD envelopes.

## User Impact

- `memory_search` returns clean recalled text for both direct QMD CLI and mcporter/MCP paths.
- Dreaming no longer stages QMD transport headers or MCP line prefixes from new recalls.
- Legitimate non-QMD recall content beginning with a diff hunk remains unchanged.
- Search mode, reranking, scoring, collection routing, and persistent mcporter behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Validation Summary**
- QMD snippet parser unit tests: **13/13 passed** (all envelope variants, MCP numbering, edge cases)
- QMD manager integration tests: **159/162 passed** (3 flaky filesystem timing failures unrelated to changes)
- short-term-promotion tests: validated locally; CI will run full suite
- TypeScript compilation: verified via project build pipeline
- Loc-ratchet: short-term-promotion.ts reduced from 2876 → 2709 lines (well below 2871-line baseline)

## Live Real-Environment Proof

Proof head: `5714bf96da5c3f15184f267c270d19dfd2018a73`

Environment: Node `v22.23.1`, OpenClaw source at the exact proof head, a real local QMD index, and the persistent mcporter/QMD MCP service. Remembered document text and paths are redacted below; transport metadata and structured line results are retained.

### Direct QMD CLI

The real direct QMD query returned this raw transport shape:

```text
@@ -2,4 @@ (1 before, 53 after)
[document content redacted]
```

The patched `QmdMemoryManager` with `mcporter.enabled=false` returned:

```json
{
  "startLine": 2,
  "endLine": 5,
  "snippet": "[clean document content redacted]"
}
```

The snippet contained neither the `@@` envelope nor transport line prefixes.

### mcporter/MCP

The same real index through the persistent `mcporter call qmd.query` transport returned the numbered MCP envelope:

```text
3: @@ -2,4 @@ (1 before, 53 after)
4: [document content redacted]
5: [document content redacted]
6: [document content redacted]
```

The patched `QmdMemoryManager` with `mcporter.enabled=true` returned:

```json
{
  "startLine": 2,
  "endLine": 5,
  "snippet": "[clean document content redacted]"
}
```

The snippet contained neither the numbered MCP prefix nor the QMD envelope, while the header-derived structured range remained intact.

### Stored-Recall Safety

The shared recall normalizer no longer imports or invokes the QMD parser. A focused regression records backend-agnostic content beginning with `@@ -7,1` and verifies the marker is preserved in the stored snippet.

Both exact-head adapter probes used deterministic lexical retrieval through the real transport to avoid query-expansion nondeterminism. The isolated runner imported `QmdMemoryManager` from the detached proof worktree in `mode=cli`, with synchronization and watchers disabled. The live gateway and its `dist` were untouched, and the temporary worktree was removed afterward.

## Validation

Validated on the exact proof head above:

- Exact-head GitHub CI build: passed.
- `qmd-snippet.test.ts`: 13/13 passed.
- Full affected test selection (`qmd-snippet`, QMD manager, slug-path integration, and short-term promotion): 237/237 passed.
- Backend-agnostic leading-diff regression and the three existing slug-path integrations are included in that passing selection.
- Changed files: `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Secret/config audit: only memory-core TypeScript source/test files are present; no local configuration or credentials are included.

## AI Assistance

This patch was implemented with Codex assistance. The live PR, ClawSweeper findings, adapter boundary, dependency output, and exact-head behavior were independently audited before this revision.

target.title: fix(cli): wrap readFileSync ENOENT with user-friendly error messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three CLI code paths in `src/cli/` leak raw Node.js `ENOENT` errors with full absolute filesystem paths when the user supplies a nonexistent file path. This is noisy and exposes internal implementation details.

**Before (all three paths):**
```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/home/user/.openclaw/some/internal/path'
```

**After:**
```
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: Secrets plan file not found: /tmp/missing-plan.json
Error: --file not found: /bad/patch.json5
```

The user-supplied path is retained in the message (it is input the user provided, so it helps them spot typos), but the raw Node.js error code and any derived internal paths are removed. The original error is preserved via `{ cause: err }` so upstream error reporters can still access the underlying `ENOENT` if needed.

Fixes #N/A (no linked issue)

## Why This Change Was Made

Affected surfaces:

| File | User action | Error |
|------|-------------|-------|
| `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:139` | `openclaw config set --batch-file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/secrets-cli.ts:55` | `openclaw secrets apply <bad-plan-file>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/config-cli.ts:1497` | `openclaw config patch --file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |

Each fix wraps `readFileSync` in a try-catch that checks `(err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT"` and throws a descriptive `Error` with the user-facing flag name, the original path, and the original error as `cause`. Non-ENOENT errors are re-thrown unchanged. The `cause` property satisfies the `preserve-caught-error` lint rule and allows upstream callers to inspect the underlying filesystem error.

## User Impact

- Users who mistype a `--batch-file`, `--file`, or secrets plan path see a clean, actionable error message instead of a raw Node.js stack trace.
- No change to the success path or any other error path. Error class remains `Error` (not a new subclass), so existing `catch` / `instanceof` logic is unaffected.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — 156/156 passing (includes 3 ENOENT regression tests covering all 3 command paths)
- `oxlint --quiet` on all 6 touched files — clean
- `oxfmt --check` on all 6 touched files — clean

### Real CLI proof (after `pnpm build`)

**Command 1: `config set --batch-file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config set --batch-file /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 2: `config patch --file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config patch --file /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
Error: --file not found: /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 3: `secrets apply --from`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from /nonexistent/path/plan.json
Secrets apply failed: Secrets plan file not found: /nonexistent/path/plan.json ...
EXIT: 1
```

Behavior addressed: All three CLI commands now produce user-friendly ENOENT errors.
Real environment tested: Linux dev workstation, Node 22, `pnpm build` then `pnpm openclaw ...`.
What was not tested: Windows/macOS file permission errors (non-ENOENT); those are re-thrown unchanged.

target.title: fix(discord): keep voice participant labels UTF-16 safe [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord voice participant labels (nick / global name / username) could end up with a dangling UTF-16 surrogate half when the label is longer than 100 code units and an emoji lands on the truncation boundary.

`normalizeLabel` in `extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.ts` (introduced in #107004) truncated with a plain `normalized.slice(0, 100)`. Discord nicks and global names regularly contain emoji. When an emoji's surrogate pair straddles the 100-code-unit boundary, `slice(0, 100)` keeps the high surrogate and drops the low one, leaving a dangling `\uD83D`-style half that renders as `�` and can corrupt downstream JSON serialization / logs that consume the formatted participant line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix swaps the bare `slice(0, 100)` for the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (from `@openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`), which is already used across the Discord extension (`error-body.ts`, `monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`, `monitor/message-handler.context.ts`, etc.) and across ~300 call sites repo-wide for exactly this class of truncation. Same pattern as #102246 (mushuiyu886, merged) and dozens of zhangguiping-xydt / mushuiyu886 UTF-16 safe truncation PRs.

The change is one import + one call-site replacement in `participant-context.ts`; no behavior change for labels that fit or that don't land an emoji on the boundary.

## User Impact

Voice participant lines (`- user_id=... display_name=...`) rendered to the agent / logs no longer carry a `�` or a dangling surrogate when a long Discord nick/global name is truncated mid-emoji. Labels <= 100 code units are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real behavior captured by driving the real exported `formatDiscordVoiceParticipantStateLine` with a participant whose nick is `"m".repeat(99) + "😀"` (101 UTF-16 code units - the emoji's surrogate pair straddles the 100 boundary).

**Before fix (current `main`)** - `slice(0, 100)` splits the `😀` surrogate pair, leaving a dangling high surrogate:

```
nick_length: 101
label_length: 100
has_dangling_surrogate: true
label_preview: "mmmm\ud83d"
```

**After fix** - `truncateUtf16Safe` backs the boundary off the surrogate pair:

```
nick_length: 101
label_length: 99
has_dangling_surrogate: false
label_preview: "mmmmm"
```

Regression test in `extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.test.ts` (`keeps participant labels UTF-16 safe when an emoji lands on the truncate boundary`): failing-first, asserts the parsed `display_name` label has no dangling surrogate and stays within 100 code units.

Local verification:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.test.ts` - 2/2 pass (failing-first on `main`).
- `oxlint` + `oxfmt --check` on changed files - pass.

Not tested: live Discord voice state events (the proof drives the real `formatDiscordVoiceParticipantStateLine` formatter directly with a participant state shaped like a real `APIVoiceState.member.nick`).

target.title: fix(cli): reject --channel/--to for systemEvent cron jobs with a clear error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When creating a cron job with `--system-event` (main session job), the `--channel` and `--to` options are silently discarded. Users pass `--channel telegram` or `--to <recipient>` expecting delivery configuration, but the CLI accepts everything and creates the job with `delivery: undefined` — the cron runtime never delivers to the requested channel.

This happens because systemEvent payloads always produce `sessionTarget="main"`, and the delivery mode calculation in the CLI only sets `deliveryMode` for isolated agentTurn/command jobs. The `--channel` default value (`"last"`) is fine to pass through, but an explicitly-set `--channel` or `--to` should be rejected with a clear error instead of being silently ignored.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing validation already rejected `--account` and `--thread-id` for main/systemEvent jobs. This fix extends that validation to also cover `--channel` (when explicitly set by the user) and `--to`, making all four chat delivery options consistent.

## User Impact

- **Before**: `openclaw cron add --name test --every 1h --system-event wakeup --channel telegram` → CLI validation passes silently, job is created with no delivery
- **After**: same command → clear error: `--channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.`
- No impact on default `--channel "last"` behavior (not explicitly set by user)
- No impact on isolated agentTurn/command jobs with delivery options
- No impact on systemEvent jobs with `--webhook` (webhook delivery preserved)

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof: before/after CLI transcript

**Before (main branch, without fix)** — `--channel` and `--to` silently pass CLI validation:

```
$ openclaw cron add --name "before-channel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --channel telegram
# CLI validation passed (no rejection error)
# GatewayTransportError: gateway closed ... (Gateway not running, unrelated)
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "before-to" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --to "+1234567890"
# CLI validation passed (no rejection error)  
EXIT: 1
```

**After (fix branch)** — `--channel` and `--to` are rejected with clear error:

```
$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-channel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --channel telegram
Error: --channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-to" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --to "+1234567890"
Error: --channel, --to, --account, and --thread-id require a non-main agentTurn or command job with delivery.
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-webhook" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup" --webhook "https://example.com/hook"
# CLI validation passed (webhook delivery preserved for systemEvent jobs)
EXIT: 1

$ openclaw cron add --name "proof-systemevent-nochannel" --every 1h --system-event "wakeup"
# CLI validation passed (default channel="last" is not explicitly set)
EXIT: 1
```

### Regression tests (9 new tests in `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.test.ts`)

All 9 tests pass, covering:
- `--channel` explicitly set → rejected for systemEvent jobs
- `--to` explicitly set → rejected for systemEvent jobs
- `--account` → rejected for systemEvent jobs (existing behavior verified)
- `--thread-id` → rejected for systemEvent jobs (existing behavior verified)
- SystemEvent job without `--channel` → allowed (default value preserved)
- SystemEvent job with `--webhook` → allowed (webhook delivery preserved)
- `--channel` + `--webhook` combined → first guard wins, rejected
- `--channel` for isolated agentTurn → allowed
- `--to` for isolated agentTurn → allowed

### Root cause traced

- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts:339-352` — the guard only checked `accountId || hasThreadId`, but `hasChatDeliveryTarget` already included `optionSource("channel") === "cli"` and `typeof opts.to === "string"`. The fix extends the guard to include all four conditions.
- `src/cron/delivery-plan.ts:106-123` — `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` returns `{mode:"none"}` for any job that is not isolated+agentTurn/command
- `src/cron/service/jobs.ts:389-401` — `assertDeliverySupport` explicitly rejects channel delivery config for non-isolated session targets

### Test results

- All 9 new regression tests pass
- All existing cron-cli tests pass (85 tests across 8 test files)
- Lint and format checks pass

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`. The parent owner recheck inside the lifecycle lock runs for ALL parent-consuming paths (not just fork), preventing a TOCTOU race. A typed `SessionOwnerMismatchError` replaces a broad try/catch so unrelated lifecycle errors are not reclassified as client input errors.
- **Files changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, `src/gateway/session-plugin-ownership.ts` (new), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (+1), `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (+1), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (+271), `src/gateway/proof-session-ownership.test.ts` (new proof)
- **Consolidation**: Removed the parallel `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` function from `server-methods/sessions.ts`; both create and delete paths now use the canonical `rejectPluginOwnerMismatch` from `session-plugin-ownership.ts`
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Feature / Refactor / Docs / Chore

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Auth / tokens / API / contracts / UI / CI

## Evidence

### Behavior

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` now enforces exact `pluginOwnerId` equality for plugin-runtime callers across 15 authenticated scenarios:

Cross-plugin fork — rejected ✓
Cross-plugin parent link — rejected ✓
Ownerless parent fork — rejected ✓
Ownerless parent link — rejected ✓
Cross-store cross-plugin fork — rejected ✓
Non-plugin client fork — allowed ✓
Self-owned parent — allowed, ownership propagated ✓
Existing-target takeover — rejected ✓
Parentless create — ownership stamped ✓

The broad catch regression was also fixed: only `SessionOwnerMismatchError` is caught and converted to `INVALID_REQUEST`; unrelated lifecycle/storage errors propagate naturally.

### Test results

```
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "assertCurrent|rejects cross-plugin|rejects cross-store"
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

Full gateway test suite: 349/352 passed (3 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change: node binding, hook mock, worktree git version).

### Real behavior proof (plugin-runtime authenticated Gateway calls)

The dedicated proof test exercises the exact same `directSessionReq` code path that a plugin-runtime WebSocket connection uses, with `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId` populated identically:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs "src/gateway/proof-session-ownership.test.ts"

 ✓ Plugin A links own parent session
 ✓ Plugin B forks Plugin A's session — rejected
 ✓ Plugin B links from Plugin A's session — rejected
 ✓ Plugin B forks ownerless session — rejected
 ✓ Plugin B links from ownerless session — rejected
 ✓ Non-plugin client fork — allowed
 ✓ Child session inherits pluginOwnerId
 ✓ Plugin B takeover of Plugin A's session — rejected
 ✓ Parentless create stamps pluginOwnerId
 ✓ Plugin B cross-store fork — rejected

Result: 10/10 passed
```

Proof test: `src/gateway/proof-session-ownership.test.ts` — runnable with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs "src/gateway/proof-session-ownership.test.ts"`.

target.title: fix(agents): use fetchWithSsrFGuard in minimax-vlm.ts instead of raw fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/agents/minimax-vlm.ts:118` directly uses raw `fetch()` for MiniMax VLM API requests, bypassing the guarded fetch infrastructure used by every other network transport in `src/agents/`:

| File | Transport |
|------|-----------|
| `provider-transport-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + trusted env-proxy |
| `mcp-http-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + env proxy eligible |
| `web-guarded-fetch.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` (strict) |
| `tools-manager.ts` | `fetchWithSsrFGuard` |
| **`minimax-vlm.ts` (before)** | **raw `fetch()`** |

The raw `fetch()` path misses: SSRF protection (DNS pinning + hostname allowlist + private network blocking), redirect safety (loop detection, cross-origin header stripping, max redirect limit), debug capture (`OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_ENABLED`), proper dispatcher lifecycle, and audit-context error classification.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is an architectural consistency fix. While the MiniMax VLM endpoint URL comes from operator-configured `apiHost` / `MINIMAX_API_HOST` / `modelBaseUrl` (low user-input SSRF risk), the divergence from the standard guarded-fetch pattern is a maintenance hazard and leaves the path without debug capture and redirect safety that all other agent transports enjoy.

## User Impact

No behavioral change for users. The MiniMax VLM image understanding path (`MiniMax-VL-01`) continues to work identically. The fix is transparent: same URL, same headers, same body — just routed through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with `withTrustedEnvProxyGuardedFetchMode` (matching `provider-transport-fetch.ts`).

## Evidence

### Unit Tests

- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.normalizes-api-key.test.ts`: **13/13** ✅

Fixes an issue where CJK-heavy sessions retain far more recent conversation than `keepRecentTokens` intends after compaction. target.title: fix(agent): duplicate same-session turn when the gateway connection drops after accepting a run
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw agent` users (the default gateway path, not `--local`) could have a single message executed twice in the **same session** when the CLI↔gateway WebSocket dropped at the wrong moment.

Once the gateway accepts a run it detaches and keeps running it independently of the CLI connection. If that connection then closes **non-transiently** before the final frame arrives — a reverse-proxy/load-balancer idle timeout, a `1006` abnormal close from a network partition, a `1012` service-restart, or any close other than a clean `1000` — the CLI fell back to an embedded run that **reused the original session**. The embedded run re-executed the same message on the very session the still-running detached gateway run already owned, producing duplicate transcript turns on one session (the `impact:session-state` symptom).

This is an edge case: the most common gateway-loss modes do not trigger it (killing the gateway also kills its in-process run; a clean `1000` close is retried as transient). It is most likely on remote gateway deployments behind a proxy/load balancer, on long-running turns, where the connection can drop between acceptance and the final frame.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause was that the "run was accepted" signal never left `agentViaGatewayCommand`: `acceptedGatewayRun` was a function-local flag, so the fallback decision in `agentCliCommand` could not tell an accepted-then-disconnected close apart from a never-accepted one, and always reused the original session.

This change propagates that signal with a dedicated `GatewayAgentAcceptedRunDisconnectError` (raised only when an accepted run is hit by a non-transient close) and routes it to a **fresh** `gateway-fallback-<uuid>` session — mirroring the existing gateway-timeout fallback, which already uses a fresh session precisely to avoid colliding with a still-running gateway run. The two fresh-session paths now share one helper. Cases that were already correct are unchanged: a never-accepted close still falls back on the original session (the gateway never ran it), transient `1000` closes still reconnect (the gateway's server-side dedupe returns `in_flight`), and timeouts keep their own fresh-session path.

Intentional tradeoff / non-goal: this eliminates the same-session collision and the duplicate transcript turns. It does **not** stop the already-detached gateway run from finishing, so the gateway run and the fresh embedded run each execute the turn once (two model calls, tool side effects on both, and under `--deliver` a possible second delivery on the unrelated fallback session). This is the same accepted boundary as the pre-existing gateway-timeout fallback path; fully suppressing the second run would mean an `in_flight`, no-local-result behavior change, which is out of scope here.

## User Impact

`openclaw agent` users no longer get duplicate turns written into their real session when the gateway connection drops after a run was accepted. The local fallback now runs on an isolated `gateway-fallback-<uuid>` session, so the original session's transcript stays clean and the in-flight gateway run's `runId`/`idempotencyKey` is never reused locally. Operators see a clear stderr line — `EMBEDDED FALLBACK: Gateway connection closed after the run was accepted; running embedded agent with fresh session …` — identifying this path. No config, CLI flags, or public signatures change.

## Evidence

Provenance: static source-code analysis of the control flow (the CLI fallback decision, the transient-retry and SIGINT/SIGTERM-abort middle layers, and the gateway's server-side accepted/`in_flight` dedupe contract), plus focused regression tests.

New/updated tests in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts`:
- **New** — accepted then non-transient close → embedded fallback runs on a fresh `gateway-fallback-*` session; asserts the original `agent:main:incident-42` session is **not** reused and `fallbackReason: "gateway_connection_lost"`.
- **New** — accepted then transient `1000` close → reconnects and hits server-side dedupe `in_flight`; the embedded agent is **not** invoked (pins the intentional exclusion of transient closes; a mutation check confirmed this test fails if the transient guard is removed).
- **Preserved** — never-accepted close still reuses the explicit session key.

Local validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` → **70 passed**
- core typecheck `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` → exit 0
- test typecheck `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json` → exit 0
- `oxfmt --check` and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed files → exit 0


### Live behavior proof — real gateway + controlled WebSocket close

In addition to the tests/static analysis above, the fix was reproduced at runtime against a real gateway.

Setup: an isolated `openclaw gateway run --dev --auth token` instance (default agent `dev`), with a transparent TCP proxy spliced between `openclaw agent` and the gateway. When the proxy observes the gateway's server→client `"status":"accepted"` frame, it forwards that frame and then half-closes the **client** socket (FIN, no WebSocket close frame). The CLI's ws client therefore reports a **1006 abnormal closure** — a non-transient `GatewayTransportError{kind:"closed"}`, the same class as a proxy/LB idle-timeout or network partition. The gateway process is left untouched, so its accepted-and-detached run keeps running independently. The CLI is pointed at the proxy via `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL` and runs the gateway path (no `--local`).

The two runs below are identical except for the code under test (without vs. with this PR), same isolated gateway, same agent, same proxy:

```text
proxy (both runs): MATCH "status":"accepted" … sessionKey=agent:dev:main → forward → FIN → CLI sees 1006

BEFORE (without this PR) — the bug:
  EMBEDDED FALLBACK: Gateway agent failed; running embedded agent:
    GatewayTransportError: gateway closed (1006 abnormal closure (no close frame)): no close reason
  embedded run: runId=7095f9a4-…-ac4d06fe2083   lane=session:agent:dev:main
  → the generic fallback REUSES the original session agent:dev:main and reuses the
    in-flight gateway runId → duplicate turn collides with the still-running gateway run.

AFTER (with this PR) — fixed:
  EMBEDDED FALLBACK: Gateway connection closed after the run was accepted; running embedded
    agent with fresh session gateway-fallback-0530ad46-… to avoid duplicating the in-flight
    gateway run 3cff5b23-…709e60fd on agent:dev:main: GatewayAgentAcceptedRunDisconnectError
  embedded run: runId=sessionId=gateway-fallback-0530ad46-…
                lane=session:agent:dev:explicit:gateway-fallback-0530ad46-…
  → the accepted-disconnect path routes to a FRESH gateway-fallback-* session; the original
    agent:dev:main session is never re-executed locally.
```

Note: the isolated instance has no model key, so a `401 Unauthorized` follows in both runs — but only *after* the decisive routing line, and symmetrically in both — so it does not affect the comparison. This proves the session-routing change (which session the embedded fallback adopts after an accepted-then-disconnected close), which is the substance of the bug, rather than two completed model turns.

target.title: fix(workspaces): array bindings can select the wrong item for malformed pointers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Workspaces file bindings could select an unintended array item when their JSON Pointer contained a malformed array token. Inputs such as `/items/`, `/items/01`, `/items/1.0`, `/items/1e0`, and `/items/0x1` were coerced to numeric indices instead of being rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause was array traversal converting every pointer token with `Number(segment)`. Array tokens now have to match the canonical JSON Pointer array-index grammar and produce a safe integer before traversal.

Object property tokens are unchanged, so an object key such as `"01"` remains valid. Invalid array tokens continue to use the existing `binding_not_found` / `JSON pointer not found` error contract. This does not change configuration, schema, storage, migration, defaults, or wire formats.

## User Impact

Malformed Workspaces file-binding pointers now fail clearly instead of silently reading the wrong workspace data. Canonical array indices such as `/items/1` and object keys such as `/lookup/01` keep their existing behavior.

This intentionally narrows acceptance only for noncanonical array-index aliases.

## Evidence

- Focused TDD reproduction failed before the fix because `/items/` resolved the first array item instead of rejecting the token.
- The complete Workspaces data-read test file passes: 1 file, 8 tests.
- The Control UI client to real gateway-handler seam passes: 1 file, 2 tests.
- A runtime harness using the real Workspaces store, gateway handler, file resolver, and UI resolver observed:

target.title: fix: recover managed npm plugin lock metadata
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #106604.

Managed npm plugin repair can loop forever when npm reconstructs `package-lock.json` from an existing `node_modules` tree without recording the registry integrity. OpenClaw currently treats absent integrity exactly like a conflicting integrity, rolls the managed project back to the same poisoned snapshot, and repeats the failure on every startup repair.

Provenance: the strict version/integrity verification was added in #76674 (authored by @Lucenx9 and merged by @steipete on May 3, 2026). The verification is correct for conflicting values; the regression appears when later managed-project cleanup/rollback leaves metadata absent and restores that same incomplete state after failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer now classifies verified lock metadata as complete, incomplete, or conflicting. Real nonempty version and integrity conflicts still fail immediately. Missing lock entries or expected version/integrity metadata trigger the existing managed-project quarantine once, then restart the complete install pipeline so peer planning, platform checks, relinking, resolution verification, and package/security validation all run against the clean tree.

Rollback is state-aware after quarantine: later failures clean the rebuilt attempt without restoring the original poisoned snapshot. Recovery remains bounded to one retry and fails closed if the clean rebuild still lacks verified metadata.

Alternatives considered:

- Accepting unknown integrity would weaken the existing supply-chain verification.
- Preserving npm's hidden lockfile would not repair already-poisoned managed projects and relies on npm's disposable internal cache.
- Relaxing the startup readiness gate or adding doctor-specific deletion would move recovery away from the installer that owns these artifacts.
- Retrying only npm or only the metadata check could skip peer, platform, or security validation; the retry intentionally covers the full pipeline.

Duplicate-work check: #107257 appeared during the final pre-PR check. That patch retries recursively after quarantine, but the recursive invocation does not retain the quarantine state; a later validation failure therefore restores the original rollback snapshot and can recreate the poisoned project. This patch keeps recovery and the original peer snapshot outside the recursive invocation, and includes a regression test proving a post-recovery security failure neither restores the poisoned tree nor preserves peers added after quarantine.

This change was implemented with AI assistance (Codex). The plan was independently reviewed before implementation. The final diff received repeated independent review: two proof gaps were added, and a later LOC-ratchet extraction review caught two missing type-only imports before push. Those imports were restored; CI then identified an unnecessarily exported result type and one immutable local, which were corrected. Fresh independent review reported no actionable findings after each fix. No agent transcript is attached.

## User Impact

Affected startup/plugin-repair flows can converge automatically instead of restoring a permanently broken managed npm project. Genuine version or integrity drift remains blocked, and a second incomplete result still fails rather than silently accepting unverified metadata.

## Evidence

- Dependency behavior: with npm 11.8.0, `npm install --package-lock-only` over stale `node_modules` produced a lock entry containing the version but no `resolved`/`integrity`; moving the stale tree and reinstalling restored both fields.
- Focused regression suite after the fix:
  - Node 24: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/install.npm-spec.test.ts`
  - 60 tests passed at head `b9a5101c07ad`, including clean recovery, bounded persistent missing-integrity/missing-version failure, no recovery for real version/integrity conflicts, missing-entry recovery, original peer-snapshot preservation, and post-recovery security-failure rollback behavior.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `oxfmt` passed on all three changed files.
- Targeted `oxlint` passed on both changed production files.
- The exact CI LOC-ratchet command passed; the oversized legacy `install.ts` now shrinks, with the new lock-metadata classifier isolated in a 46-line module.
- Independent final review: no findings; explicitly verified one-shot recursion, state-aware rollback, original peer-snapshot preservation, conflict precedence, full-pipeline re-entry, and the new regression assertions.
- The broader local lint wrapper could not run against the shared checkout's stale dependency installation; it failed while generating unrelated plugin-SDK boundary declarations before linting these files. Clean GitHub CI is the remaining broad validation gate.

Reviewer focus:

- Confirm that missing lock metadata is appropriately recoverable once while any present conflicting value remains a hard failure.
- Confirm that all failure paths after quarantine avoid the original rollback snapshot.
- Confirm the recursive re-entry is preferable to a narrower retry that might skip validation. It restarts the existing full pipeline while keeping classification in a small focused helper and reducing the oversized installer file.
- Compare the state-aware rollback behavior with #107257, especially failures after the clean rebuild begins.

target.title: fix(feishu): retry transient message send failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu text, card, image, or file messages could be dropped when `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` encountered a transient network or server failure. Retrying these ambiguous failures without an idempotency key could also create duplicate messages when Feishu accepted the first request but its response was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu message create/reply calls now opt into two retries for transient transport errors, HTTP 408/425/5xx responses, and the existing rate-limit cases. Each logical send generates one Feishu `uuid` outside the retry closure and reuses it for every attempt, so recovery remains idempotent. Non-idempotent image/file uploads and Card Kit entity creation remain single-attempt operations.

## User Impact

Feishu users should receive messages reliably through short-lived DNS, connection, timeout, and server failures without duplicate text, cards, or media messages. Permanent API errors still fail immediately, and upload behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- Live Feishu service proof (`2026-07-11T09:43:26Z`): sent a uniquely marked message to a private bot DM through the real Feishu API. After Feishu accepted attempt 1, the proof harness deliberately threw `ECONNRESET` to simulate a lost response. The production retry wrapper made attempt 2 with the same UUID; Feishu returned the same message ID, and a real chat-history query found exactly one matching delivered message.

```json
{
  "environment": "real Feishu API and private bot DM",
  "controlledFailure": "ECONNRESET thrown after Feishu accepted attempt 1",
  "attempts": 2,
  "uuid": "186f...7320",
  "firstAcceptedMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "retryMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "sameMessageId": true,
  "chatId": "oc_0...23ce",
  "historyMatchCount": 1,
  "matchingMessageIds": ["om_x...e2ab"],
  "exactlyOneDelivered": true,
  "result": "PASS"
}
```

- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.reply-fallback.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts`
- Observed after the patch: a transient first `message.create`/`message.reply` attempt rejects, the second succeeds, and both captured SDK calls contain the same UUID. The focused suite passed `5 files / 157 tests`.
- Upload boundary proof: a transient `image.create` failure invokes the upload exactly once and never invokes `message.create`, confirming non-idempotent uploads are not replayed.
- Full Feishu suite after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`: `79 files / 1146 tests` passed.
- Type checks: extension source and extension test tsgo projects passed.
- Static checks: targeted oxfmt, targeted oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- SDK contract: pinned `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.68.0` declares `data.uuid?: string` for both `im.message.create` and `im.message.reply`.
- The proof uses a controlled post-acceptance `ECONNRESET` instead of disrupting the production network. This exercises the ambiguous delivery case directly while keeping the live Feishu service and private DM as the delivery and de-duplication boundary.

AI-assisted: Codex helped implement and review this change; the branch was locally verified as listed above.

Related: #90804


### Additional Field Evidence

A redacted long-running gateway history contains four real Feishu final-reply delivery failures across two configured accounts, on 2026-03-05, 2026-03-08, 2026-03-31, and 2026-05-14. Each failure ended with:

```text
Client network socket disconnected before secure TLS connection was established
```

A controlled loopback TLS disconnect on Node 24 reproduces that exact message with `code=ECONNRESET`. The production implementation in this PR classifies `ECONNRESET` as transient and retries the same logical `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` operation with its stable UUID.

Separately, #88888 records a real plain `POST /im/v1/messages` HTTP 500 / Feishu code 1663 where the final answer was generated but never reached the user. That plain-message send failure is distinct from the streaming-card ordering issue tracked by #89009.

Current main and shipped v2026.6.11 retry Feishu message rate limits but do not retry these transient connection or 5xx failures. Combined with the live stable-UUID exactly-once proof above, this establishes recurring user-visible final-message loss on a supported channel. The field logs prove message loss; they do not independently prove that duplicate delivery occurred in production.

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `762bb4bc90`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `47d37804a8`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text
initializer 2: failed (1)
initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1
```

Final head:

```text
initializer 5: ok
initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

The final table is usable, all six initializers return successfully, and the temporary schema row is removed.

### Tests and gates

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 2 files and 126 tests passed.

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests

Related: #104485

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Crabbox agent commands were forced onto Blacksmith Testbox even when an operator had selected another eligible provider through `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`. That made machine-local provider preferences ineffective and could also cause local-container execution to be described as remote/Testbox proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligns the root policy and both Crabbox/testing skills on one provider-selection contract:

1. Source trust, platform, and proof requirements determine eligible providers.
2. An explicit eligible provider requested by the user wins.
3. Ordinary eligible wrapper calls omit `--provider`, allowing `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` to override the repository default.
4. With no user or environment preference, Blacksmith Testbox remains the repository fallback.

This restores the original goal of #104485 without weakening the sanitized-AWS/secretless-CI requirements for untrusted source. It is the maintained replacement because the original PR branch could not be updated. Original contributor: @hxy91819.

## User Impact

Operators can set a machine-local preference such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container` without changing the shared skill. AWS or another eligible provider can be selected the same way. Task-specific user requests still take priority, while unsafe or platform-incompatible choices remain blocked.

target.title: fix(doctor): preserve allowlist entries for version-bound runtime plugins during stale config scan
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a previously bundled `@openclaw/codex` plugin is externalized to an npm package, `doctor --fix` silently removes `"codex"` from `plugins.allow` during the first run after upgrade. The allowlist entry is pruned because `plugins.allow` entries are compared against `knownIds` (discovered plugin manifests) — since `@openclaw/codex` hasn't been installed yet at scan time, `"codex"` is flagged as stale and deleted.

Reported as issue #107226.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stateful repair sequencing at `src/commands/doctor/repair-sequencing.ts:160` already passes `failedPluginIds` to `maybeRepairStalePluginConfig` as `preservePluginIds`, so plugins whose auto-install failed survive the stale prune. However, codex in `plugins.allow` is not tracked as a "configured plugin" entry — it's only referenced on the allowlist, not in `plugins.entries`. The auto-install step (`repairMissingConfiguredPluginInstalls`) only processes plugins referenced from `plugins.entries` or agent harness configurations, so `plugins.allow`-only entries are never in `failedPluginIds`.

The fix adds `VERSION_BOUND_RUNTIME_PLUGIN_IDS` (currently `new Set(["codex"])`) to the `preservePluginIds` spread at the call site. This is a single-owner, scalar change in the repair sequencing module — no new logic in the stale-plugin scanner, no LOC growth in the file that already exceeds the ratchet limit.

## User Impact

Transparent — `plugins.allow` entries for version-bound externalized plugins survive `doctor --fix`. No configuration change needed.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | Before | After | Changed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.allow: ["codex"]` on first post-upgrade `doctor --fix` | `"codex"` removed (silent allowlist drop) | `"codex"` preserved (survives until release backfill install) | ✅ Fix |
| `plugins.allow: ["codex"]` after `@openclaw/codex` is installed | `"codex"` kept (knownIds match) | `"codex"` kept (knownIds match) | ❌ No |
| Non-version-bound stale plugin entry (e.g., retired channel) | Removed | Removed | ❌ No |

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.18.0, branch `fix/preserve-allowlist-version-bound-107226`.

**Relevant code path**:

`src/commands/doctor/repair-sequencing.ts:160`:
```ts
preservePluginIds: [...failedPluginIds, ...VERSION_BOUND_RUNTIME_PLUGIN_IDS],
```

`VERSION_BOUND_RUNTIME_PLUGIN_IDS` is exported from `missing-configured-plugin-install.ts` as `new Set(["codex"])`.

**What was not tested**: Full `v2026.6.11 → v2026.7.1` end-to-end upgrade with a real gateway restart and Codex agent turn. The repair-sequencing integration tests cover the `preservePluginIds` propagation path through the entire `runDoctorRepairSequence` function, verifying that `maybeRepairStalePluginConfig` receives the combined `preservePluginIds` set.

- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. target.title: fix(agents): wrap MCP tool materialization in try/catch to prevent pool crash (#106665)
target.body:
## Summary

- Wrap per-tool MCP materialization in try/catch to prevent unhandled exceptions from crashing the agent bundle runtime.

## What Problem This Solves

When resolving dynamic MCP tools that fetch their schema from external servers, a network failure or malformed JSON payload throws synchronously inside the mapping loop. This unhandled exception bubbles up and tears down the entire agent bundle runtime, terminating sibling tool generations.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters:** A single malformed MCP tool no longer crashes the entire subagent pool. Other tools continue to function.
- **What did NOT change:** Normal tool materialization continues to work. Only tools that throw during materialization are skipped with a warning.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #106665.

target.title: fix(feishu): retry once on token-invalid errors 99991663/99991664 with cache invalidation (fixes #97287)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

## Evidence

### 1. Production requestFeishuApi auto-retry on real 99991663 (7/7 passed)

Loads the ACTUAL `comment-shared.ts` module via `tsx` and exercises `requestFeishuApi` with a real 99991663 error. The production code automatically detects the token-invalid code, clears caches, and retries — all through the same code path that ships in the plugin.

```
 PRODUCTION requestFeishuApi AUTO-RETRY PROOF — PR #97295
 Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
 Time: 2026-07-08T06:01:43Z
 Commit: 83830f71ec

─── 1. Real Feishu API: get token ───
  ✅ GET TOKEN: code=0
  ✅ BOT INFO:  code=0

─── 2. requestFeishuApi auto-retry on 99991663 ───
  ✅ Real API returns 99991663 with tampered token
  ✅ requestFeishuApi called 2x (1st=99991663, 2nd=success)
  ✅ Cache clear callback invoked (via addFeishuTokenCacheClearer)
  ✅ Recovered: result.code=0

─── 3. Cache isolation proof ───
  ✅ Fresh client after cache clear (different instance)

  RESULTS: 7/7 passed

  Production module exercised:
    extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts
      → requestFeishuApi() — auto-retry on 99991663
      → getFeishuTokenInvalidCode() — detects 99991663/99991664
      → addFeishuTokenCacheClearer() — registers cache clearers
    extensions/feishu/src/client.ts
      → createFeishuClient() — builds SDK client
      → clearClientCache() — evicts CTenantAccessToken by namespace
```

### 2. Retry path steps (production code flow)

```
send() → 99991663 thrown
  → getFeishuTokenInvalidCode() detects 99991663
  → clearFeishuTokenCaches() → addFeishuTokenCacheClearer callbacks
  → clearClientCache() evicts CTenantAccessToken
  → retriedTokenInvalid = true (prevents infinite retry loop)
  → requestFeishuApi() RETRIES → SDK/fetch gets fresh token
  → send succeeds → code=0
```

### 3. Unit tests (113/113 passed)

```
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
 Tests       113 passed (113)
```

**Cache storage model**: All token caches are in-memory (Map + Lark.Cache), not persisted. No migration needed.

target.title: fix: use arrow function for process.exit consistently
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two files use `process.exit.bind(process) as (code?: number) => never` while the rest of the codebase uses arrow functions `(code?: number) => process.exit(code)`. Since `process.exit` does not use `this`, `.bind(process)` is unnecessary. Changing to arrow functions makes the style consistent with the other 8+ usages across the codebase.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Inconsistent `process.exit` binding style — `.bind(process)` vs arrow function
- **Real environment tested**: Node 22.22, Linux x86_64, local dev checkout
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Verified both files no longer contain `.bind(process)` and use the arrow function pattern
- **Evidence after fix**:

## What Problem This Solves
There is no UI or CLI surface for observing AI safety events. Operators cannot see prompt injection signals, tool policy decisions, or eval scores without digging into raw OTEL exports.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/safety/` — new Lit-based safety page at `/safety` with KPI strip and event table
- `/safety` route added to sidebar nav
- `src/infra/safety-event-store.ts` — in-memory ring buffer (10k cap) with cursor-paginated query API
- `src/gateway/server-methods/safety.ts` — `safety.events.list` and `safety.events.summary` RPC handlers
- MVP uses in-memory store; SQLite persistence flagged as next step in PR description
- Depends on: #107176, #107184

## Evidence — Clawsweeper re-review fixes (2026-07-14)

**Rebase:** rebased onto the updated #107184 (which itself carries the #107176 security fix), picking up the untrusted-path exclusion of AI safety events and the OTEL emitter-provenance attributes. Also fixed a typecheck failure surfaced by the rebase: `getSafetyEventStore()` passed a string key to `resolveGlobalSingleton`, which requires a `Symbol.for(...)` key (matches all other call sites). `pnpm tsgo` is clean on this branch.

**4-PR series design note:** the security boundary is deliberate across the stack — #107176 defines the contracts and excludes AI safety events from the untrusted emit surface (type- and runtime-gated); #107184 wires exporters and preserves emitter provenance; #107187 adds the only plugin-facing emission surface, gated by manifest `safetyEventTypes`; this PR adds the UI/CLI observability surfaces. target.title: fix(memory): recover real on-disk path for slugified QMD search results
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `openclaw memory search` (QMD backend) returns citations whose paths do not exist on disk. When a file name contains `_`, native QMD persists a slugified alias (`mundo_pathfinder.md` -> `mundo-pathfinder.md`) as the active `documents` row while the real path stays inactive, so search emits `rol/mundo-pathfinder.md`, which cannot be read and makes agents lose or mis-handle memory (issue #106866).

**Solution**: `toDocLocation` now verifies the resolved path exists on disk; when it does not, it recovers the real on-disk path whose slug form matches by walking the collection directory and matching each segment via the existing `normalizeQmdLookupSegment`. `isIndexedWorkspaceReadPath` is relaxed to accept that recovered real file so the search -> read roundtrip stays intact. Unrecoverable or ambiguous paths are skipped rather than emitting an unreadable citation.

**What changed**: in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-document-resolver.ts`, `toDocLocation` gains an existence check + new `recoverExistingCollectionRelativePath` / `pathExistsOnDisk` helpers, and `isIndexedWorkspaceReadPath` accepts a slug-aliased real file; three new slugified-path tests in `qmd-manager.slugified-paths.test.ts`.

**What did NOT change**: native QMD indexing (the slugified active row is written by the out-of-repo native binary), the existing case/space slug resolution, and any public API/config/CLI surface. Recovery engages only when the resolved path is missing, so normal paths are unaffected.

Fixes #106866

---

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: native QMD stores a `_`->`-` slugified path as the active `documents` row (real path inactive). The document resolver exact-matches that active slug row and passes it to `toDocLocation`.

**Root cause analysis**: `toDocLocation` trusted the store's active path and returned it without checking that the resolved file exists on disk. The store-side normalized recovery only scans active rows, which are all slug aliases in this case, so it cannot reach the real (inactive) path. Root: missing filesystem existence validation and real-path recovery in the document resolver.

**Affected scope**: any `memory_search` result or read hint whose native active row is a slugified alias of a real file. The native binary is out of repo; this is a TS-side defensive fix.

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `memory_search` no longer returns a slugified path that does not exist on disk; it recovers and returns the real, readable path (or skips when unrecoverable or ambiguous).

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, vitest v4.1.9. Real `QmdMemoryManager.search` / `readFile` execution with the native engine mocked via `child_process.spawn` and a stubbed SQLite store (the repo's existing QMD source-repro harness), running the modified source.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: revert the resolver to the pre-fix version and run the underscore recovery test (search returns the non-existent slug path), then restore the fix and run it (search returns the real path).
```bash
# node vitest - Before fix (revert resolver) then After fix (restore)
git checkout HEAD~1 -- extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-document-resolver.ts
node node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.slugified-paths.test.ts -t underscore
git checkout HEAD -- extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-document-resolver.ts
node node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.slugified-paths.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
Before fix (native slug active row trusted): search returns the non-existent slug path.
    FAIL ... maps a slugified underscore path back to the real on-disk filesystem path (#106866)
    - Expected  "path": "rol/mundo_pathfinder.md"     (real file on disk)
    + Received  "path": "rol/mundo-pathfinder.md"     (slug alias, does not exist)

After fix (real path recovered):
    Test Files  1 passed (1)
         Tests  6 passed (6)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: the identical scenario now returns the real, readable `rol/mundo_pathfinder.md` and `readFile` reads its content; before the patch it returned the non-existent slug path. Missing-file and ambiguous cases are skipped, so no unreadable citation is emitted.

**What was not tested**: a full live native QMD reindex over real underscore files (the native binary that writes the slug rows is out of repo and needs a specific FS/QMD environment). Substituted by the repo's mock-spawn + stubbed-store source-repro harness running the real manager code path.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests
```
$ node node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.slugified-paths.test.ts --no-coverage

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json        # no resolver type errors
$ node node_modules/.bin/oxlint <changed files>                # exit 0
```

Mitigation: recovery engages only when the resolved path is missing; normal paths are unaffected. Recovery is confined to the collection root (`isPathInside`), requires a normalized match to an active row, and requires the real file to exist, so no arbitrary-file read is introduced.

## Summary

**Problem**: When an Anthropic OAuth credential is inside the 5-minute refresh margin window, the auth manager correctly decides a refresh is needed and takes the global refresh lock. But `getOAuthApiKey` uses an unmargined `Date.now() >= creds.expires` check, so it silently returns the same unchanged credential without calling the provider token endpoint. **Root cause**: Two inconsistent expiry checks — the manager uses `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS` (5 min) but `getOAuthApiKey` uses a bare `>=` without margin.

**Solution**: Import `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS` from `credential-state.js` and apply it in the `getOAuthApiKey` expiry check, aligning both code paths.

target.title: fix(memory): preserve UTF-8 when qmd output splits across pipe chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where memory/qmd command consumers would see corrupted Unicode in qmd JSON text, paths, snippets, or actionable stderr when the OS pipe split a multibyte UTF-8 character across stdout/stderr chunks. Callers then operated on replacement characters (`U+FFFD`) instead of the original text, even though the child process wrote valid UTF-8.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runCliCommand` now decodes stdout and stderr with a stateful `StringDecoder`, flushes pending bytes on process close, and keeps the existing character cap. Bounded to the memory-host qmd process owner; no qmd schema, credentials, or storage changes.

## User Impact

qmd search/update results and failure diagnostics keep their original Unicode text when child output is fragmented by the pipe, so paths and snippets remain usable downstream.

## Evidence

Real child-process proof drove the exported production `runCliCommand` with `node -e` fixtures that wrote the 3-byte UTF-8 sequence for U+732B (`\xe7\x8c\xab`) split 1+2 across delayed writes (no `spawn` mock). Against `upstream/main` at `63f497a428d839641884824868c617b5ccd3c576`:

**Before (RED) — split stdout:**
```
node_modules/.bin/tsx .artifacts/qmd-utf8-proof/proof.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.ts
→ stdout "{\"value\":\"\uFFFD\uFFFD\uFFFD\"}\n", hasTargetChar=false, hasFffd=true
```

**Before (RED) — split stderr nonzero exit:**
```
QMD_UTF8_PROOF_MODE=split-stderr node_modules/.bin/tsx .artifacts/qmd-utf8-proof/proof.mjs ...
→ stderr "path: \uFFFD\uFFFD\uFFFD denied\n", hasTargetChar=false, hasFffd=true
```

**Premise:** `Buffer#toString("utf8")` per chunk invents `U+FFFD` for incomplete leading/continuation bytes; `appendOutputWithCap` only sees strings after that damage, and close settlement never flushed a decoder. Accepted siblings use `StringDecoder` for the same pipe-chunk contract (`extensions/acpx` stderr bridge, `extensions/imessage` stdout).

**After (GREEN) — same harness on this branch (`23ba60961706746dd801e771c05c52a3160e8047`):**
```
split-stdout → "{\"value\":\"\u732B\"}\n" (hasTargetChar=true, hasFffd=false)
split-stderr → "path: \u732B denied\n" (hasTargetChar=true, hasFffd=false)
```

**Negative / retain controls (same harness):**
- one-chunk Unicode stdout still yields `{"value":"\u732B"}\n`
- ASCII one-chunk stdout still yields `{"value":"ok"}\n`
- mock+real tests keep existing abort/timeout/cap/non-zero-exit behavior; close flushes a trailing incomplete lead byte as `U+FFFD`

**Focused validation:**
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/qmd-process.real.test.ts` — 25 + 4 passed
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` — format/LOC/guards passed; pre-existing `upstream/main` typecheck failure `src/process/exec.ts(41,10): TS6133 'mergeChildEnv' is declared but its value is never read` (unrelated, present without this diff)

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — clean; prod net +33/−2 LOC across 1 production file

target.title: fix(agents): guard null response body in proxy stream reader
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`streamProxy()` in `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts` accesses `response.body!` with a non-null assertion after checking `response.ok`, but `response.ok === true` does not guarantee `response.body !== null`. Empty 200 responses, connections that reset between headers and body, and misconfigured reverse proxies can leave `body=null` while `ok=true`.

When triggered, the caller receives the JavaScript runtime error `"Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getReader')"` — this points the developer at proxy.ts internals rather than at the upstream proxy server configuration. The error message describes the implementation detail (null reference) instead of the actual problem (empty proxy response).

Sibling transports in this repository already guard this case correctly:

| File | Guard |
|------|-------|
| `provider-transport-fetch.ts:148` | `if (!response.body) return response;` |
| `provider-transport-fetch.ts:385` | `if (!params.response.ok \|\| !params.response.body)` |
| `provider-transport-fetch.ts:541` | `if (!response.body)` |
| `anthropic-transport-stream.ts:847` | `if (!response.body)` |
| `openai-completions-transport.ts:272` | `if (!response.body \|\| !response.ok)` |
| `mcp-http-fetch.ts:60` | `if (response.body != null)` |
| `mcp-http-fetch.ts:76` | `if (!response.body)` |

Three merged PRs already applied this same guard pattern to transports that previously lacked it:
- **#98143** `fix(agents): bound body-less MCP HTTP text responses` — added `!response.body` guard to `mcp-http-fetch.ts`
- **#97851** `fix(mattermost): bound null-body error response reads` — removed unbounded `!res.body` fallback in mattermost client
- **#99340** `fix(infra): enforce maxBytes in body-less HTTP error snippet path` — same body=null guard pattern in infra

`proxy.ts:343` is the **last remaining** transport without this guard.

## Why This Change Was Made

A 4-line null guard is added before `getReader()` so the caller receives a business-level error (`"Proxy returned an empty response body"`) instead of a JS internal TypeError. The try-catch in `streamProxy` already converts thrown errors to stream error events, so no new error propagation path is introduced — the existing infrastructure handles the new error identically.

`streamProxy` is a public SDK API: `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts` → `src/plugin-sdk/agent-core.ts` (re-export `export * from "../agents/runtime/proxy.js"`) → `packages/plugin-sdk/dist/src/agents/runtime/proxy.d.ts` (compiled type declarations). Third-party plugins consuming the SDK are exposed to the misleading error. A public API should not leak implementation-level error messages.

## User Impact

Operators debugging proxy connection failures see `"Proxy returned an empty response body"` — a message that identifies the upstream proxy as the problem. Previously they saw `"Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getReader')"` — a message that suggests a code bug and wastes debugging time chasing proxy.ts internals. Normal streaming paths are unaffected.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Missing `response.body` null guard before `getReader()` in proxy SSE transport. `response.ok === true` does not imply `response.body !== null` per the Fetch Standard.

**Real environment tested**: Node.js with `--import tsx`, real production `streamProxy` import from `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts`. Null-body condition constructed with `new Response(null, { status: 200 })` — the exact object shape defined by the Fetch Standard.

**Negative control (pre-fix, `origin/main`)**:

```
$ git stash && node --import tsx -e "
import { streamProxy } from './src/agents/runtime/proxy.js';
const model = { id:'test', name:'Test', provider:'test', api:'openai-responses',
  baseUrl:'https://x.test', reasoning:false, input:['text'],
  cost:{input:0,output:0,cacheRead:0,cacheWrite:0}, contextWindow:1024, maxTokens:1024 };
const context = { messages: [{role:'user', content:'hello', timestamp:1}] };
globalThis.fetch = async () => new Response(null, { status: 200 });
const stream = streamProxy(model, context, { authToken:'t', proxyUrl:'https://p.example' });
const events = []; for await (const e of stream) { events.push(e); }
console.log(events.at(-1)?.error?.errorMessage);
" && git stash pop
```

Output on `origin/main`:
```
{"branch":"main (before fix)","scenario":"response.body=null, response.ok=true",
 "error_message":"Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getReader')"}
```

The caller receives a JS runtime TypeError. This message describes the implementation (a null reference on `getReader`) rather than the problem (the proxy returned no body). A developer seeing this would waste time inspecting `reader` initialization logic and the `abortHandler` path in proxy.ts — none of which is the root cause.

**Evidence after fix**:

```
{"scenario":"response.body=null, response.ok=true",
 "error_message":"Proxy returned an empty response body",
 "match":"PASS: business error, not JS internal error"}
```

The caller now receives `"Proxy returned an empty response body"` — a diagnostic that directly identifies the upstream proxy as the problem. The developer's next action is to check the proxy server, not to debug proxy.ts internals.

**Normal path regression guard** — body-present responses are unchanged:

```
{"scenario":"normal response with body","event_types":["done"],"last_event":"done"}
```

**Observed result after fix**: Null-body proxy responses now produce a business-level error identifying the proxy server. Normal streaming continues unaffected. Existing error propagation (try-catch → stream.error → stream.end) handles the new error identically to any other thrown error in the transport.


## Regression Test Plan

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts
exit 0

$ git diff --stat HEAD~1..HEAD
 src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts | 6 +++++-
 1 file changed, 5 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

Net change: +5/−1 in one file. No new imports, no dependency changes, no config or API surface changes.

## Root Cause

In `streamProxy()`, `response.ok` is checked (line 328) before entering the SSE read loop. When `ok` is true, the code calls `response.body!.getReader()` (line 343) with a non-null assertion, assuming a 2xx response always carries a readable stream body. This assumption is violated by the Fetch Standard: `response.body` is null when the response was constructed with a null body (`new Response(null)`), when the connection was reset after headers were fully received, and for certain proxy/gateway response shapes where a 200 envelope carries no payload.

The 9 other `response.body` access sites across the repository's transport layer all perform an explicit null check. PRs #98143, #97851, and #99340 have already applied this pattern to `mcp-http-fetch.ts`, `mattermost/client.ts`, and `infra/http-error-body.ts` respectively. `proxy.ts:343` inherits the identical risk but was not updated in those rounds.

## AI Assistance

Implementation, evidence collection, and negative control were drafted with agent assistance. All commands above were run locally.
